intro: Needle Drop finds the right song for a scene, and tells you whether you are actually allowed to use it. There is one field, and everything else appears only when you need it.
describe: Describe a scene. A small language model, running locally, turns it into a structured music brief.
fast1: While it works, an agent writes the brief, searches more than twenty thousand Creative Commons tracks, and checks every license. On this small CPU that takes a few minutes, so we are speeding it up.
shortlist: Tracks you can actually use stand out. The rest fade back. The asterisk means the license was checked against a 2019 snapshot, so confirm before you publish.
picks: Tap plus on any track for why it fits, the license text it cites, and what it costs.
trace: Every run is traced, with steps, tokens and spend. Running locally, that spend is zero.
use: Verdicts follow your intended use. For monetized video, non-commercial and no-derivatives tracks are never marked cleared.
clipdrop: Or drop a clip anywhere on the page. This sample has hard cuts, rain, and subtitles.
fast2: The clip goes through cut detection, audio tempo, subtitles and keyframe captions, and then the same agent loop. This is the slowest step on a small CPU, because the local model has to read everything it found before it can write the brief.
analysis: The analysis reports pacing, cuts, tempo and palette, and feeds them into the music brief.
play: Tap a title to drop the needle, and it plays against your clip. Here a stand-in tone plays, because this sandbox can not reach Jamendo.
rate: Rate whether it fits, and those labels calibrate the judge.
review: There is also a labeling screen with keyboard shortcuts, for quick review.
github: The code, the evals, and honest notes on what is verified are on GitHub. Thanks for watching.
